title: Open, vendor-neutral track deduplication, correlation and blue-force drone identification for drone-dense tactical air pictures below the fire-control tier (with cross-fabric provenance/catalog)
scoring_notes: Scores are analytical heuristics, not facts. Evidence labels: FACT / INFERENCE / HYPOTHESIS with confidence. Verified this session via web search: DefenseScoop 2026-09-23 (Falcon Peak 26.2: Lattice deployed as 'digital backbone and baseline standard against which all commercial sensor-to-shooter counter-UAS assets are measured', Yuma Proving Ground, 31 Aug-25 Sep 2026, https://defensescoop.com/2026/09/23/northern-command-falcon-peak-26-2-counter-drone-exercise/); SENSEI Data Fusion Correlator remains an RFI (released 2026-02-12, due 2026-03-20, EMC2 for NSWC) with no public RFS or award found (https://www.emccrane.org/portfolio-items/sensei-data-fusion-correlator/; https://nta.org/2026/02/17/sensei-data-fusion-correlator/) - public evidence insufficient on progression. Other claims rely on the G05 evidence card and E07 regulatory findings (E07-F3, F7, F13, F19, F21, F25, F30) from earlier stages. IDIQ ceilings ($20B EA) are not revenue; the $87M task order is obligated-ceiling for Anduril, not addressable spend for a challenger.

scores.rationale: Fratricide of friendly drones and engagement delay under time pressure are safety-critical; MWI (West Point) analysis flags friendly/enemy drone confusion as a fratricide driver (FACT, MEDIUM) and Ukrainian reporting claims ~50% of downed drones were lost to own EW/AD before ID systems (secondary claim, euro-sd 2025-11, MEDIUM). Not 5 because no documented US fratricide incident or formal US requirement for a neutral layer surfaced; US evidence is doctrine (JICO manual dedup), RFIs and exercise anecdotes.

Occurs on every c-UAS engagement decision and every friendly drone sortie near a sensor; frequency is rising with 12,080 Gauntlet drones accepted and drones-to-every-squad intent (Army Times 2026-09-18, RECALL, MEDIUM). Not 5 because at most US sites today drone density and sensor overlap are still exercise-level rather than continuous combat conditions.

Adjacent budgets are large (Army C-sUAS cumulative $2.6B requested through FY2025 per GAO-25-107491, 2025-06-17, FACT HIGH) but the card states no line item exists for an independent correlation/provenance layer; the only named money for the neutral/blue-object problem is a $500k DIU/INDOPACOM prize pool (2025-12-10) and an undisclosed-value Navy SENSEI correlator RFI. Budget for this function is inside incumbent C2 awards (Lattice $87M task order, FAAD C2 sustainment).

Vehicles exist (JIATF-401 CSO via ACC-Detroit Arsenal, EMC2 OTA, DIU, xTech/SBIR, C-UAS marketplace with export-control vetting) but none has issued a requirement for a vendor-neutral cross-fabric correlator; the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER chain breaks at requirement owner (fragmented across JIATF-401, CPE Missiles & Space, Navy SENSEI, AFRL, PM LAV, each buying fusion inside its own stack).

Track-to-track association (MHT/JPDA, covariance intersection) is textbook, but slow, low-RCS, clutter-heavy small-UAS tracks at 4-10 Hz with <2% false merges is a specialist problem and the blue-ID half depends on cooperative signals that fail in contested EMS; feasible for a team with a tracking specialist, not for generalists (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Card's PoC estimate ($150k-300k for a bench demo with commercial sensors and one contract tracking engineer, INFERENCE) consumes the entire founder stake and yields only a bench result; a credible military demo is $1M-2.5M and sponsor-gated. $250k buys a data-collection rig and a plugin, not a defensible product.

Unclassified bench/range demo in 3-6 months is plausible, but a demo the government would score (real sensor mix, CUI exercise captures, host-C2 integration) is 12-18 months plus clearance/export plumbing per the card's killer_risk; incumbents can ship the equivalent feature inside that window.

Phase 1 data is self-generated with commercial sensors/drones plus academic anti-UAV datasets and Remote ID/ADS-B (available); Phase 2 validation data (labelled multi-sensor small-UAS tracks with ground truth, real friendly-flight logs, UC2/Link 16 logs) is CUI/Secret and sponsor-gated, and export-controlled CUI is effectively US-person-only (E07-F30, MEDIUM).

Score of 1 because the product's value is realised only when it consumes FAAD C2/Lattice interface specs, military sensor track formats and exercise data that are likely ITAR technical data or CUI; the identity half drifts toward IFF/AIMS/NSA keying policy; fielding needs an ATO inside a host-C2 accreditation; SBIR requires >50% US-citizen/PR ownership (E07-F3, FACT HIGH); FOCI treats both founders as foreign interests (E07-F19). Constraints to scope with counsel, not legal conclusions.

ATAK-CIV/TAK SDK is open-source government-owned (E07-F25, FACT HIGH), commercial c-UAS sensors, drones and Remote ID receivers are purchasable, and synthetic 50-200 track scenarios can be generated; both founders can work on this phase. Not 5 because the unclassified phase cannot prove the numbers the government scores.

Score of 1 because the government has already anointed the seam's owners: Lattice is JIATF-401's common tactical C-UAS C2 ($87M task order 2026-03-13, Defense One 2026-03-14, FACT HIGH), leads the NGC2 common data layer (Breaking Defense 2026-06, RECALL) and was used at Falcon Peak 26.2 as the 'baseline standard' for all commercial sensor-to-shooter assets (DefenseScoop 2026-09-23, verified this session); FAAD C2 (Northrop) covers Army SHORAD with its own correlator and fratricide mitigation; Raft holds NGC2 registries; a SENSEI correlator vendor, sensor-side fusion vendors (Hidden Level, Dedrone/Axon) and drone-IFF hardware vendors crowd the rest.

Score of 1 because Anduril and Northrop own the entity model, the customer relationship and (for Lattice) a public SDK/partner program that pulls new feeds into their stack; adding friendly-drone telemetry ingestion and provenance metadata is a feature release for them (card incumbent_response, INFERENCE MEDIUM). Only structural vulnerability is the government's lock-in anxiety and the incumbents' lack of motive to audit their own fusion quality - a real but unfunded opening.

CoT/TAK is open and government-owned (low barrier), but the interfaces that matter for the JIATF-401 and Army SHORAD markets are Lattice's Anduril-controlled SDK (access terms not public) and FAAD C2's Northrop-developed internals; UC2 governance unverified; Link 16 needs a gateway. Per-buyer re-integration risk is high (INFERENCE, MEDIUM).

Algorithms are well-known literature; the durable assets (labelled multi-sensor small-UAS data, validated integrations, accreditation history, 'chosen neutral auditor' status) all require sponsor access this team cannot secure quickly; provenance/catalog is sticky only after fielding.

Airports, stadiums, prisons, utilities and DHS/FAA test sites share the duplicate-track and 'is that our inspection drone?' problem and Remote ID (ASTM F3411) provides open cooperative data; but civil C-UAS is crowded with integrated vendors (Dedrone/Axon) with built-in fusion, budgets are smaller and US civil C-UAS authorities are gated (card rates dual-use 'medium', INFERENCE).

Allied mixed-vendor stacks (NATO/UK SAPIENT-style interfaces, EU JRC C-UAS fusion group, Ukraine's acute problem) are a more natural home for a neutral correlator than a US market that just picked Lattice; provenance/catalog could generalise to other track domains and the JICO tier. Expansion is real but each step is a different customer, jurisdiction and export regime.

Pattern to date is one correlator bought per program (FAAD C2, Lattice, SENSEI) then absorbed and sustained inside that C2; a fielded neutral layer could earn per-site licences and sustainment, but no evidence of a repeatable cross-program purchase pattern exists (Navy track-fusion SBIR topics recur 2011-2025 without closure, RECALL MEDIUM).

Score of 1 because four of the card's expertise roles are 'fatal if absent' and none is present: multi-target tracking/data-association engineer, former C-UAS/JICO operator, TAK/UC2 integration engineer, export/FOCI/SBIR counsel; the Indonesian founder (non-US person) cannot touch the ITAR/CUI data the product needs (E07-F13, F30), neither founder is clearance-eligible for years (E07-F21), and a 50/50 cap table fails the SBIR ownership test (E07-F3). The German founder's PR status helps for ITAR but not for FOCI or clearances. Not legal advice.

market.summary: No program element or budget line funds an independent correlation/provenance layer; the seam was just handed to Lattice ($87M task order under a $20B ceiling, Mar 2026) and FAAD C2; SENSEI's correlator RFI is a program-specific buy, not a cross-fabric standard; named neutral-layer money is a $500k DIU prize pool; buyers are fragmented with no single requirement owner; the non-US-person co-founder implies 12-18 months of access plumbing during which incumbents absorb the feature. Analyst assessment: sustained - the budget and requirement-owner links of the chain are absent, and this session's search found no RFS or award following the SENSEI RFI.

competition.summary: Falcon Peak 26.2 (Sept 2026) used Lattice as the 'baseline standard' against which all commercial sensor-to-shooter C-UAS assets are measured; Anduril's public SDK/partner program makes 'post into Lattice' the natural path for any new sensor or friendly-drone feed; Northrop covers SHORAD; Raft holds NGC2 registries; Navy solves its own gap in-house. Analyst assessment: sustained - the Falcon Peak claim was verified this session (DefenseScoop 2026-09-23) and the government's revealed preference is consolidation, not a neutral broker. One caveat: an exercise benchmark role is not the same as a production mandate, and JIATF-401 still runs open demos, so a plug-in role beside Lattice remains possible but unfunded.

feasibility.summary: Incumbent absorption is the documented current state; ITAR/FOCI/clearance rules wall off Phase-2 validation data from this team; $250k buys only a bench PoC while a credible military demo costs $1M-2.5M and the SBIR bridge is constrained by ownership and foreign-national rules; the core tracking specialist is absent; correlation historically gets bought once per program and absorbed. Analyst assessment: sustained - the founder-fit criteria (6-10, 18) average 2.0 and the two lowest scores (regulatory 1, team fit 1) are exactly this skeptic's points.

verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 4 and I cannot show they are wrong. The decisive reason is a broken value chain: PROBLEM (real, severe, frequent) -> USER (C-UAS operators, ADAM cells, JICOs) is intact, but REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE breaks at the requirement-owner and budget links. No JIATF-401, Army, Navy or USAF office has written a requirement for a vendor-neutral, cross-fabric correlation/identity/provenance layer; the card itself says no line item exists; and the government's most recent revealed preference (Lattice designated common tactical C-UAS C2 in Mar 2026, NGC2 common data layer lead in Jun 2026, and 'baseline standard' at Falcon Peak 26.2 in Sept 2026 - the last verified this session) is to consolidate correlation inside one vendor's stack and pull third-party feeds into it through that vendor's SDK. The strongest bull evidence - the SENSEI Data Fusion Correlator RFI (Feb-Mar 2026) - shows a program buying a bespoke correlator for its own system, and this session found no RFS or award following it (public evidence insufficient). Independently of the market, founder fit is 2.0: the fatal-if-absent tracking specialist, operator/JICO advisor and TAK/UC2 integrator are all missing, the non-US-person co-founder cannot access the ITAR/CUI interface specs and exercise data the product's value depends on, and $250k funds only a bench PoC whose numbers the government will not score. A major penalty is applied for the broken chain. The gap is a real operator pain that the government is choosing to solve by consolidating around incumbents, and absence of a neutral layer is not evidence anyone will pay for one.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not recommended as a company for these founders, but if pursued at all the only survivable slice is the skeptics' convergent narrow version: (1) an unclassified, TAK-CIV-based 'friendly-flight declaration' adapter (MAVLink/GCS -> CoT extension carrying flight window, geometry and intent) that makes any host C2's blue-ID better rather than replacing its fusion, plus (2) a post-mission, government-owned provenance/after-action audit tool that ingests exported track and engagement logs to reconstruct which sensor said what, when, and why a track was labelled friend/unknown, sold as JIATF-401's or the JICO community's independent oversight tool. This avoids the live-fusion seam the incumbents own and targets the one function they are unmotivated to build. It is a single-digit-buyer niche with no identified budget, so it should be treated as a 4-8 week sponsor-validation test (does a named JIATF-401 or AMD official say they would fund it?) rather than a capital commitment. Civil/range C-UAS sites (DHS/FAA test sites, airports, stadiums) are the only fully unclassified beachhead, and that market is crowded.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today they should not build the broad vendor-neutral correlator; it fails because the buyer has already chosen where correlation lives (Lattice for JIATF-401/NGC2, FAAD C2 for Army SHORAD) and nobody funds a neutral layer, so the demo would prove a capability the customer has decided to get from an incumbent. The only thing worth building first is a cheap falsification test of the narrow version: a TAK-CIV plugin plus edge service that (a) ingests two or three commercial c-UAS feeds (low-cost radar or RF detector, EO/IR tracker, Remote ID/ADS-B) and declared friendly flights from a MAVLink GCS, (b) emits merged tracks with per-source lineage over CoT, and (c) produces a replayable after-action 'who said what, when, and why it was called friend/unknown' record; run it on a self-collected range dataset with scripted commercial drones and 50-200 synthetic tracks, reporting dedup rate, false-merge/false-split rate, latency at 10 Hz and blue-ID precision/recall with cooperative signals removed. They would show it to JIATF-401 technical staff at an open industry demo, the AFRL counter-drone lab (Mar 2026 RFI), a 4ID/25ID NGC2 experimentation lead, and one civil C-UAS test site (DHS/FAA), asking one question: would you pay for an independent audit of your fused picture and a standard friendly-flight declaration your C2 vendor does not control? The customer would care only if lock-in anxiety or a fratricide near-miss has made 'auditable, government-owned provenance' a stated need; an incumbent cannot trivially crush the audit role because Anduril and Northrop are structurally unmotivated to grade their own fusion, but they can trivially crush the adapter and the live correlation by shipping the same ingestion as a Lattice/FAAD C2 feature, which is why only the audit slice has any defensibility. The milestone that would justify $2-5M is not a demo metric but a procurement fact: a named requirement owner (JIATF-401 acquisition cell, CPE Missiles & Space or the SENSEI sponsor) issuing a CSO topic, RFS or SBIR/xTech topic that explicitly asks for a C2-independent correlation/provenance capability, paired with a sponsor-provided CUI exercise capture and a US-person engineering enclave (with a hired tracking specialist and export/FOCI counsel already in place) so the team can prove false-merge rates on real data. Absent that fact within 6-9 months, the founders should redeploy the capital to a gap with an identifiable requirement owner and budget line.
bear_case_summary: The seam is real but already owned: the government designated Lattice as the common tactical C-UAS C2 (Mar 2026), NGC2 common data layer lead (Jun 2026) and 'baseline standard' at Falcon Peak 26.2 (Sept 2026); FAAD C2 covers Army SHORAD with its own correlator and fratricide mitigation; both incumbents can ship blue-drone ingestion and provenance as a feature release faster than a two-founder team can obtain CUI data. No requirement owner or budget line exists for a neutral layer; SENSEI's correlator is a one-program buy still at RFI stage; the only named neutral-layer money is a $500k prize pool. Founder fit is poor: fatal-if-absent roles are missing, the Indonesian founder cannot access ITAR/CUI interface data, neither founder is clearance-eligible for years, and $250k funds only a bench PoC.
bull_case_summary: Pain is severe and rising: friendly-drone density is exploding (12,080 Gauntlet drones by Sept 2026), Ukraine documented heavy drone fratricide and fielded UA DroneID, MWI recommends friendly-UAS IFF, doctrine institutionalises manual dedup (JICO/Joint Track Data Coordinator), and Navy track-fusion SBIR topics have recurred for 14+ years. The government demonstrably buys correlation as a separate component (SENSEI Data Fusion Correlator RFI, Feb 2026) and pays startups for blue-object integration (DIU/INDOPACOM, Dec 2025); UDRA policy demands provenance/catalog attributes the tactical mesh lacks; lock-in anxiety around a $20B Lattice enterprise agreement could create demand for a government-owned neutral auditor; allied mixed-vendor stacks (NATO SAPIENT-style interfaces, EU JRC fusion group, Ukraine) are a more natural home for a neutral correlator. The unclassified Phase 1 is buildable by both founders on open TAK-CIV and commercial hardware.
